column1: # Bare text and the punctuation characters.
# A BARE STRING HOLDS LETTERS, DIGITS, `-` AND `_`, AND NOTHING ELSE. Every
# other punctuation character is either syntax where the grammar gives it
# alias name, `=` after one -- or an error where it does not. Never
# silently part of a string: `x=y`, `6/2`, `50%` and `>10` were all bare
# strings once, each a well-formed wrong document, and each is refused
# now with `bare_punct` naming the character. A value that needs one is
# `-` and `_` are text, which makes `team-payments`, `2026-09-05` and an
# `a-b` key legal bare; `-` at the START of a run is still the sign of a
# number and the negation prefix, and `+` is still the sum.
# ... beyond the first plane too: a letter is text, a symbol is not.
# ... and only there: a `+` after the marker with no digit after it is
# the sum, of the two strings `1e` and `x`.
# THE REFUSALS, one per character the old lexer absorbed into text.
# A pair in list position is held to the same key rule: `[x=y: 1]` is
# refused, not generated as the element `{"x=y":1}`, and pathed through
# The refusal names the character and points at it.
# Quoted, every one of them is a value.
